latest_release.body:
<!-- generated-release-notes v1 -->

The `NOT_STARTED` workflow run status is removed in this release. The upgrade command converts any runs in that state to `ENQUEUED` automatically. Update any custom integrations, filters, or views that reference `NOT_STARTED` before upgrading.

A regression from 2.61 is fixed for team members without the Applications permission. Those members were seeing an empty sidebar — Companies, People, Opportunities, Tasks, Notes, and Dashboards all gone. Navigation is restored for those roles.

Emoji reactions now work in direct messages. Email thread panels no longer break when channel visibility is enabled. Internally, workflow privacy moves from a visibility enum to a boolean flag; the old column stays this release and is dropped in 2.63.

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- The NOT_STARTED workflow run status is removed. The upgrade converts existing NOT_STARTED runs to ENQUEUED. Update any integrations, filters, or views that reference NOT_STARTED before upgrading. ([#31154](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31154)) by @charlesBochet

## 🌟 Highlights

- The NOT_STARTED workflow run status is removed; existing runs are converted to ENQUEUED on upgrade. ([#31154](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31154))
- Team members without the Applications permission can see their sidebar items again after the 2.61 regression. ([#31179](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31179))
- You can now react to direct messages with emoji. ([#31013](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31013))
- Email thread panels no longer break when channel visibility is enabled on a workspace. ([#31163](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31163))

## ✨ New features

- Emoji reactions now work in direct message threads, not just channels. ([#31013](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31013)) by @Bonapara
- The AI navigation tool can now insert built-in sidebar sections such as Channels and Recent chats, not only custom ones. Requires IS_CUSTOMIZABLE_SIDEBAR_ENABLED. ([#31014](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31014)) by @thomtrp

## 💅 Improvements & UX

- Workflow privacy is now stored as a boolean (isPrivate) instead of a visibility enum. The old column remains this release and is dropped in 2.63. ([#30962](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/30962)) by @Weiko
- Channels are created from the + button in the section title only. The separate Add channel row below the list is removed. Requires IS_CUSTOMIZABLE_SIDEBAR_ENABLED. ([#31017](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31017)) by @thomtrp
- The Teams bot now responds when unavailable, sends a welcome message on install, and handles help requests. Behind IS_CHAT_ASSISTANT_RELEASED. ([#31143](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31143)) by @abdulrahmancodes
- The Make Private and Share with Workspace workflow menu actions now read from the new isPrivate field instead of the deprecated visibility column. ([#31184](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31184)) by @Weiko

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Clearing a section or tab name while editing no longer snaps back to the previously saved name. Requires IS_CUSTOMIZABLE_SIDEBAR_ENABLED. ([#31033](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31033)) by @thomtrp
- Teams message content is only stored after the sender is confirmed as a workspace member. Messages from unrecognized senders no longer leave text in the workspace. Behind IS_CHAT_ASSISTANT_RELEASED. ([#31145](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31145)) by @abdulrahmancodes
- Email thread panels and participant columns no longer break when channel visibility is enabled on a workspace. ([#31163](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31163)) by @charlesBochet
- Team members without the Applications permission now see Companies, People, Opportunities, Tasks, Notes, and Dashboards in the sidebar. These were lost after the 2.61 upgrade. ([#31179](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/31179)) by @thomtrp

## 🔧 Developer & API

- Legacy message visibility hooks

# Why Twenty Twenty gives technical teams the building blocks for a custom CRM that meets complex business needs and quickly adapts as the business evolves. Twenty is the CRM you build, ship, and version like the rest of your stack. Learn more about why we built Twenty
# Installation ### Cloud The fastest way to get started. Sign up at [twenty.com](https://twenty.com) and spin up a workspace in under a minute, with no infrastructure to manage and always up to date. ### Build an app Scaffold a new app with the Twenty CLI: ```bash npm install -g twenty twenty app init my-app cd my-app yarn install ``` Define objects, fields, and views as code: ```ts import { defineObject, FieldType } from 'twenty-sdk/define'; export default defineObject({ nameSingular: 'deal', namePlural: 'deals', labelSingular: 'Deal', labelPlural: 'Deals', fields: [ { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: FieldType.TEXT }, { name: 'amount', label: 'Amount', type: FieldType.CURRENCY }, { name: 'closeDate', label: 'Close Date', type: FieldType.DATE_TIME }, ], }); ``` Then ship it to your workspace: ```bash twenty auth login --url https://your-workspace.twenty.com twenty app publish --private ``` See the [app development guide](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/getting-started) for objects, views, agents, and logic functions. Building with a coding agent? Install the official [Twenty app skills](./packages/twenty-agent-skills), which work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and any other harness supported by the `skills` CLI: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/tree/agent-skills --list ``` The `agent-skills` branch is created by the first successful publish from `main`. Until then, use the [local build instructions](./packages/twenty-agent-skills#local-development). [`SKILLS.md`](./SKILLS.md) explains the other skill families in this repository and who they are for. ### Self-hosting Run Twenty on your own infrastructure with [Docker Compose](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/self-host/capabilities/docker-compose), or contribute locally via the [local setup guide](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/contribute/capabilities/local-setup).

# Everything you need Twenty gives you the building blocks of a modern CRM (objects, views, workflows, and agents) and lets you extend them as code. Here's a tour of what's in the box. Want to go deeper? Read the User Guide for product walkthroughs, or the Documentation for developer reference.
